newsitem.title: UK: Soldier injured in clash with N.Ireland mob.
newsitem.headline: Soldier injured in clash with N.Ireland mob.

text.p: A soldier was injured in Northern Ireland on Wednesday evening in a clash with a mob throwing petrol bombs, Britain's Press Association (PA) news agency reported.
It said police and British Army soldiers replied by firing plastic bullets at the crowd in Lurgan, south of Belfast.

PA said the police and troops had been trying to search a section of the railway line between Belfast and the Irish capital Dublin, when they were attacked by youths hurling stones who were later joined by the petrol bombers.
It said the crowd of around 150 had come from a nearby largely Catholic estate.
The soldier was hurt in the face.
The section of the Belfast to Dublin rail line running through Lurgan had been shut for several days following a bomb scare.
Tension has been rising in Northern Ireland in recent days since a Protestant organisation vowed to hold a march in the town of Londonderry, which Catholics in the area regard as provocative.

Last week, the Irish Republican Army (IRA) set off two car bombs inside Britain's army headquarters in Northern Ireland in its first attack in the province in two years. The IRA is fighting for a united Ireland.
Its pro-British Loyalist rivals indicated this week they would not retaliate, as had been feared, by ending a two-year ceasefire.
